comparator.name: Bachelor Pedagogische Wetenschappen
comparator.sourceNotes: Source-first completion 20 October 2026. Adopted ESSB EER 2026–2027 Appendix III E p.44 confirms 17 unique credited components, three 60-EC years, an open 15-EC minor and compulsory 22.5-EC bachelor project. Retain the first-listed Pedagogiek route and its 15-EC pedagogical support option; the mutually exclusive school-development option is assessed as another target-supported direction, not stacked into the pathway. Appendix I D pp.32–33 defines academic inquiry into upbringing, education, contextual intervention and pedagogical research. Current programme and study pages corroborate the scope. The root decision was absent; this v2 decision explicitly recovers the verified external choices and records a newly adjudicated academic exception. The original positive composition and previous findings are preserved in review evidence. The programme brochure at its reused URL now says 2027–2028, so it supports illustrative examples only and does not control 2026–2027 credits.

programmes.label: Bachelor Pedagogische Wetenschappen at Erasmus University Rotterdam

exception.reason: The tested 24-course UCR programme has genuine developmental, clinical, cognitive and social-science strengths, including child assessment, a youth-resilience project and teaching-design work with primary-school children. It does not sustain the defining academic inquiry into upbringing, parenting support and educational practice that connects the Erasmus curriculum. Replacing general biomedical, cognitive and contextual courses with the strongest plausible social-policy, ethics and communication additions still does not establish that programme-level inquiry. The conclusion concerns substantive comparability, not degree-title equivalence, a matching-course quota or professional accreditation.
exception.curriculumContext: Complete 17-component, 180-EC Pedagogiek pathway independently verified against the adopted 2026–2027 EER, including 15-EC open minor and compulsory 22.5-EC bachelor project. No external-curriculum blocker remains.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Read the original 24 selected courses and screen the 151-course enriched workbook, blob c2bcc3b63ec7831fd0f7b8ddfb32de1260521655. Strongest positive: HCBPSYC314 covers attachment, childhood and personality across the lifespan; HCBPSYC212 includes disorders from infancy onwards; HCBPSYC312 explicitly includes child/adolescent assessment and psychotherapy, a stronger connection than the short cached description implies. MCCCOMM213 teaches didactic skills and actual design/delivery of public-speaking exercises with schoolchildren aged 9–12, including disadvantaged pupils. HCBPSYC315 creates evidence-based materials for youth leaders and educators in a school-culture/resilience project. HCBCOGN312 covers language acquisition, reading and dyslexia; methods courses support real empirical and synthesis skills. These are substantive contributions, not dismissed as incidental. However, the original programme remains organised around psychology/neuroscience and adult human biology rather than continuing inquiry into upbringing, family-school relationships, pedagogical theory, education design and related intervention/research. Tested bounded repairs add GOSPOLI312 public-policy analysis, GOSPHIL212 ethics, GOSLAWJ111 human rights, GOSSOCI111/214/311 social contexts, MCCCOMM111 as rhetoric foundation and GOSHIST311 boarding-school histories. Their actual content supplies general policy, ethical, social and historical inquiry, not an integrated academic study of parenting support or educational systems. Expanding one school project into a programme-wide claim or assuming a child-focused brief for a general research project would invent content. For the alternative Onderwijswetenschappen direction, school-based rhetoric, language learning and youth resilience remain real but do not supply sustained educational theory, school development or education-policy analysis. No defensible Alternative 1 established; later alternatives are not manufactured.

candidateAssessment.assessment: Strong developmental and child-clinical courses plus school/youth projects support parts of the field. A broader psychology programme cannot stand in for sustained upbringing, parent support and pedagogical-context intervention; bounded substitutions do not repair that gap.

candidateAssessment.concept: Learning, educational opportunity and school development
candidateAssessment.assessment: MCCCOMM213 genuinely designs and delivers school exercises; HCBCOGN312 covers language acquisition and dyslexia; HCBPSYC315 works with educators. General sociology, policy and statistics complement these, but the combined catalogue does not establish a continuing programme in education theory, school development and educational-policy practice. Other-route interests are legitimate evidence for the generic target but do not change the neutral external-route choice.

audience.programmeDescription: Pedagogical Sciences at Erasmus University Rotterdam studies how children and young people develop, learn and grow up within families, schools and communities. The programme combines theories of upbringing and education, developmental psychology, research methods and practical work. The pathway shown takes the Pedagogiek option in pedagogical support.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers relevant study in developmental and clinical psychology, language learning, youth resilience and work with primary-school children. These courses do not together provide a sufficiently close programme in upbringing, parenting support and education. We therefore show the Erasmus curriculum without proposing a UCR alternative.

curriculum.limitation: The pathway includes a 15-EC minor and a compulsory 22.5-EC bachelor project. The final-year pedagogical support option is shown; the alternative education-sciences option is not combined with it.
